record.original_question: Do short-baseline and other neutrino anomalies—LSND and MiniBooNE antimuon-to-antielectron appearance, reactor antineutrino disappearance, gallium calibration deficits, possible differences between neutrino and antineutrino oscillations, low-energy MiniBooNE excesses, possible seasonal variations, and OPERA's reported superluminal muon-neutrino velocity—represent real physics beyond standard three-flavour neutrino oscillations, and if so can a single theory explain them quantitatively, for example by sterile neutrinos, CPT violation, or nonstandard matter interactions, while satisfying the existing oscillation and Lorentz-invariance constraints?

evidence.quote: However, there exist results which do not fit this picture and may suggest that the fourth (or, maybe, even the fifth) neutrino exists.
Other anomalies. Recent intense exploration of the field of neutrino oscillations revealed also a range of other anomalies which are currently being discussed and rechecked intensively.
All these very interesting anomalies currently await their confirmation in independent experiments.

These scenarios experience considerale difficulties with simultaneous explanation of the full set of the experimental data, though they cannot be totally excluded; it might happen that a certain combination of these possibilities is realized in Nature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model extended by neutrino masses, the three known active neutrino flavours (electron, muon, tau) mix via a 3×3 unitary PMNS matrix and undergo oscillations governed by two independent mass-squared splittings Δm²_21 ≈ 7.5×10⁻⁵ eV² and |Δm²_31| ≈ 2.5×10⁻³ eV². A number of experimental results sit uncomfortably with this three-flavour picture, including: (i) the LSND excess of ν̄_e appearance in a ν̄_μ beam at L/E ~ 1 m/MeV; (ii) the MiniBooNE ν_μ→ν_e and ν̄_μ→ν̄_e appearance excesses, including a low-energy excess; (iii) the reactor antineutrino anomaly, a deficit of order 6% in measured ν̄_e fluxes at baselines ≲100 m relative to flux predictions; (iv) the gallium anomaly, a deficit observed in calibrations of radiochemical solar-neutrino detectors with ⁵¹Cr and ³⁷Ar sources; (v) possible asymmetries between neutrino and antineutrino oscillation parameters; (vi) reported seasonal variations in some neutrino data sets; and (vii) the OPERA report of superluminal muon-neutrino propagation.

The problem is the following: determine whether all of these effects (or some specified subset) can be quantitatively accommodated by a single extension of the three-flavour framework — for example, a model with one or more sterile neutrinos (3+1, 3+2, or 3+1+decay schemes), CPT-violating neutrino mass spectra, or non-standard neutrino matter interactions — that simultaneously
(a) reproduces all signal regions of the listed anomalies within their reported uncertainties,
(b) is consistent with all existing null short-baseline disappearance and appearance limits (including from MINOS/MINOS+, IceCube, KARMEN, MicroBooNE, Daya Bay, PROSPECT, STEREO, BEST follow-ups, and KATRIN), and
(c) respects laboratory and astrophysical Lorentz-invariance and CPT bounds.

Construct such a model and exhibit the parameter values that achieve a global fit of acceptable statistical quality, or prove that no model in a specified class can do so.
artifact.status_search_result: The OPERA superluminal-neutrino result was retracted (timing-system error) shortly after 2011. The simplest 3+1 sterile-neutrino interpretation of the short-baseline anomalies is now strongly disfavoured: MicroBooNE (2025) excludes nearly the entire LSND/MiniBooNE-preferred region, and KATRIN (2025) sets stringent limits on eV-scale sterile mixing. Reactor and gallium anomalies show internal tension within 3+1 fits. However, the underlying anomalies (gallium deficit, MiniBooNE low-energy excess) remain unexplained, and broader/decaying-sterile and non-standard-interaction models are still being explored. Hence the global question is partially settled (some explanations excluded) but no single accepted model fits all data.

status_evidence.title: MicroBooNE finds no evidence for a sterile neutrino
status_evidence.snippet: MicroBooNE excludes nearly the entire favored region in which a single sterile neutrino could be hiding.
status_evidence.claim: The minimal 3+1 sterile-neutrino explanation of LSND/MiniBooNE is largely ruled out.

status_evidence.title: Sterile-neutrino search based on 259 days of KATRIN data
status_evidence.snippet: KATRIN sets improved limits on eV-scale sterile-neutrino mixing using 259 days of tritium beta-decay data.
status_evidence.claim: Direct kinematic searches further constrain sterile neutrino parameters.

status_evidence.title: Broad sterile neutrinos and the reactor/gallium tension
status_evidence.snippet: Reactor and gallium short-baseline data are in tension within the standard 3+1 sterile scenario.
status_evidence.claim: Reactor vs. gallium anomalies cannot be jointly fit by a simple 3+1 model.

status_evidence.title: Decaying Sterile Neutrinos and the Short Baseline Oscillation Anomalies
status_evidence.snippet: Models with decaying sterile neutrinos are proposed to reconcile the anomalies with disappearance bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Extended sterile-sector models remain under active investigation.
